newsitem.title: USA: Fraud charges face Cambridge Biotech ex-CFO.
newsitem.headline: Fraud charges face Cambridge Biotech ex-CFO.

text.p: The former chief financial officer of Cambrige Biotech Corp. was charged Wednesday with securities fraud after a federal investigation found that he falsely inflated the Worcester, Mass.-based company's revenues.
The company, which changed its name to Aquila Biopharmaceuticals and brought in new management, had no comment on the action against Peter Hartman, 53, its former CFO.
Hartman, who lives is Swansee, Ga., is accused of grossly exaggerating the revenues for the maker of diagnostic tests that were contained in the company's public filing and press releases.

"Today's charges represent the third time in the past 18 months that a publicly traded Massachusetts company has been implicated in a 'revenue recognition' scheme," First U.S. Assistant Attorney Mark Pearlstein said in a statement.
"For all of their preceived complexity, such schemes are nothing more than an attempt to rip off the investing public by misleading them about a company's financial performance.
"This case illustrates that 'cooking the books' is a recipe for prosecution," Pearlstein said.

Hartman and others at CBC conducted a scheme to overstate the company's revenues by improperly recognising revenue from sales that were not legitimate, according to the federal information filed Wednesday.

The company routinely included in its revenue figures sales in which the customer had not agreed to buy the product. The scheme started in May 1991 and continued through June 30, 1993 with the filings of false Securities and Exchange Commission reports, the court papers said.
If convicted, Hartman faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 fine.
